title: Hunt by any alias
text: The threat group field takes ATT&CK names and aliases alike: Cozy Bear, Midnight Blizzard and APT29 all find the same group.

title: Browse the last 30 days of CVEs
text: Under the CVE field, Browse the last 30 days lists new CVEs newest first. Filter to Exploited (KEV), your technology stack or CVSS 7+, and pick several to hunt them together.

title: Researched CVEs start at once
text: A CVE marked Researched in the 30-day browser has already had its NVD record, advisories and proof-of-concept exploits read, so its hunt skips straight to building detections.

title: Appliance CVEs need network queries
text: No EDR runs on a PAN-OS, Ivanti or Citrix appliance, so for those CVEs the exploit-request and IOC-sweep queries are the ones that can see an attack. Make sure your proxy, WAF or appliance logs reach the SIEM.

title: Hunt a technique across every group
text: Enter technique IDs instead of a group (T1003, T1021.001) and Shikari builds detections from every group's procedure examples for them. A parent technique also takes its sub-techniques' examples.

title: Merge by Parent Technique
text: Tick Merge by Parent Technique, beside the threat group field, to fold T1003.001 and T1003.002 into T1003 before correlating, so correlations are by technique rather than by sub-technique.

title: Fill ATT&CK's gaps with OSINT Comparison
text: About 318 ATT&CK techniques name no indicator at all. OSINT Comparison builds detections for those from public SecOps, Sentinel, Splunk and Elastic rules, and scores each of yours against them.

title: LOL datasets add real command lines
text: With LOL datasets on, LOLBAS, LOLDrivers and LOLRMM entries for the binaries, drivers and RMM tools a group uses go into its queries, and each detection links to the entries it used.

title: Set your technology stack
text: Hunts leave out techniques and procedures that can't happen in your estate once Environment → Technology stack is set. The Threat Feed and the CVE browser use it too. Tick Ignore it for this hunt to use all of ATT&CK.

title: Generate only for the SIEMs you run
text: Tick your SIEMs under Profile → Environment → SIEM platforms and every hunt, upload and report generates for those alone, which saves time on every run.

title: Stop the AI question
text: After Generate, tick Remember this choice on the AI question to stop being asked. Profile → API Keys → Hunt prompt brings it back.

title: Defanged indicators are fine
text: Analyse recognises defanged indicators such as evil[.]com and hxxp://, so you can paste a report as published.

title: Untick the vendor's own domains
text: Analyse shows every TTP and IOC it found before generating. Untick vendor domains, sinkholes and techniques mentioned only in passing so the IOC sweep stays clean.

title: Add your own known-good list
text: Put internal domains in bespoke/mappings/known_good.json, with the same keys as Shikari's own list, and the IOC sweep will never hunt for them.

title: When a URL gives nothing
text: Some sites block automated fetches or draw their text with JavaScript. Save the page as PDF or text and upload the file to Analyse instead.

title: IP and domain indicators expire
text: IPs and domains in an IOC sweep expire 90 days after Shikari first saw them, and the sweep's description gives the date. Regenerate drops the expired ones; hashes and files never expire.

title: Hunt what several groups share
text: On Research, Consolidate Techniques and turn on Shaded rows: a technique used by more than one of your groups is the best value for a detection. Hunt Techniques then hunts each one once.

title: Who targets my country?
text: On Research, enter a country and switch between Attributed and Targeted: groups from that country, or groups that have targeted it.

title: Profile your own domain first
text: Profiling your own company shows what an attacker sees before they act, ranks the groups likely to target you, and Add to my technology stack fills Environment from what it found.

title: Pick the groups on the review
text: After a company profile, each of the ten ranked groups on the review has its own tick box, with the top three ticked. Generate detections runs a hunt for each one ticked.

title: Is your domain spoofable?
text: On the exposure map, the Mail node says whether SPF, DMARC and DKIM are published and enforced. A domain is flagged spoofable unless SPF fails unknown senders and DMARC quarantines or rejects.

title: Close the earliest gaps first
text: A Results page's Threat briefing ranks gaps by how early they come in the attack, then by how many correlations they're part of. It's worked out without AI.

title: Chains are high-confidence leads
text: A correlation with + between three techniques is a chain: all three on one host within the window. It fires far less often than a pair, so treat it as a high-confidence lead next to its pairs.

title: X-SIEM pivots
text: A chain that spans two of your SIEMs becomes an X-SIEM pivot: each stage's query where that telemetry lives, and the host, user, IP and hash fields to join them on inside the window.

title: Rearrange an attack flow
text: Drag cards between tactics, drag the dot on a card's edge to draw a link, and hold Option or Alt to place a card freely. STIX downloads the flow as you left it, for the CTID Attack Flow Builder.

title: Attack flows from the keyboard
text: Focus a card and press Alt with the arrow keys to move it along its tactic or to the next one. ⌘/Ctrl-Z undoes any change.

title: Remap a detection, with a reason
text: Change a detection's technique or tactics with a comment and it's badged Mapping changed. Hover for ATT&CK's default; Restore default puts it back. Coverage shows it with a dashed amber outline.

title: Find the detections that can't fire
text: Tick the tables or event types you actually ingest under Profile → Config → SIEM data sources. Detections that need anything else are badged Source not ingested and kept out of git and SIEM pushes.

title: Point Splunk at your indexes
text: Splunk index, sourcetype and field names vary by estate. Profile → Config → SIEM field mapping saves your own schema, which the generator reads instead of the CEF defaults.

title: Diff two ATT&CK releases
text: Export a group's run to git before and after a Regenerate, then diff the two commits on Detections as code to see exactly which queries a new ATT&CK release moved.

title: One hunt for a whole campaign
text: Detections as code → Master hunt query turns a run's Defender XDR detections into one advanced hunting query that ranks devices by how many of the run's techniques they show.

title: Coverage gaps between SIEMs
text: Coverage → Coverage gaps lists techniques your saved detections cover in some of your SIEMs but not all, with a column and a gap count per SIEM: useful mid-migration, or when two teams run different SIEMs.

title: Teach Shikari your house style
text: Production-tested queries in bespoke/llm_references/ become templates and examples for generation, and Coverage's Reference queries layer shows what they cover.

title: Tag detections in bulk
text: In the Library, tick detections and use Manage Tags to label them by use case, owner or deployment state.

title: Watchlists collect for you
text: Save a Threat Feed search as a watchlist (a group, a CVE, a vendor) and Shikari collects by itself, every six hours by default, with new matches badged on the Intel menu. Email me sends them on.

title: The Threat Feed hides what you don't run
text: Posts that name only products outside your technology stack are tagged Not your stack and left out of the default view. They're still under All.

title: From a Threat Feed post to detections
text: Analyse in Shikari on any Threat Feed card opens Home → Analyse with the post's URL filled in.

title: Search research without leaving your machine
text: Search all research looks through every post Shikari has collected, back to 2016 for some sources, and ATT&CK. Untick Include web news to keep the search off Google and Bing.

title: Hunt from a TAXII collection or MISP
text: Indicator Management imports a STIX bundle, a TAXII collection or recent MISP events as a hunt input, and exports a finished run back out. Credentials are used for that request only, never stored.

title: Who has reported this indicator?
text: Intel → Indicator Management searches the last seven days of vendor, CERT and government, news and aggregator reporting for an IP, domain, URL, hash, email or CVE, defanged or not. The tier chips narrow the sources.

title: Update only what ATT&CK changed
text: MITRESaw's Update collects only the groups the latest ATT&CK release changed. Full rebuild collects every group in about 30 minutes, which a new indicator exclusion needs to reach them all.

title: Your country on the map
text: Set Profile → Country and it's green in every Cyber Powers view. The Targets view shows how many ATT&CK groups are described as targeting it.

title: Will your detection see it?
text: Emulate checks your detections' indicators against attacks recorded in public labs, and shows which logs captured each technique, before you build a lab of your own.

title: Run the plan in MACAT and VECTR
text: An emulation plan exports as a MACATable TOML, and the Threat library's test cases do too, so MACAT can run them and push the results to VECTR.

title: Logged but no alert
text: In an assessment, a blue outcome of logged, no alert offers a detection hunt for that technique: the telemetry is there, only the detection is missing.

title: Assessment results in ATT&CK Navigator
text: Export an assessment as an ATT&CK Navigator layer, shaded by blue outcome from not logged through to prevented.

title: Groups ATT&CK doesn't know
text: Hunting a name ATT&CK doesn't know opens Manual. Enter one technique per entry with the commands, paths and registry keys that were seen: they become the query's indicators.

title: Elastic regex matches the whole value
text: Elastic's regexp has to match the entire field, so mimikatz alone only matches a value that is exactly mimikatz. The Regex page flags it and shows the pattern written for each SIEM.

title: Windows paths in a regex
text: C:\Windows\cmd.exe in a regex never matches as written: \W means "not a word character". The Regex page catches single backslashes and unescaped dots before the query reaches the SIEM.

title: Let an agent fix only what's flagged
text: The Detection repair agent runs the static and precision checks over a run, fixes only what they flag, re-checks each fix and saves it with a reason. Changes wait for your approval by default.

title: Ask Shikari with a local model
text: Ask Shikari can answer from a local model (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp) set under Profile → API Keys, so questions about your detections never leave the machine.

title: Script Shikari with an API token
text: Profile → Security → API Tokens issues a token for the console, the MCP server and your own scripts. Set SHIKARI_TOKEN instead of a password; it works with MFA.

title: Use Shikari from any MCP client
text: shikari mcp exposes Shikari's hunts and agents to an MCP client such as Claude Code, so an assistant can hunt, check queries and read your Library.

title: Sections remember being open
text: Results, Library and Coverage sections start collapsed. Open the ones you use and they stay open next time.

title: Latest run or all runs
text: On a Results page, Showing: Latest run / All runs switches between the newest run of a group, report or CVE and every run of it combined.
